blocks.text: Jenny’s apartment roof had a view of Cleveland that made Seth forget the stairs. Terminal Tower rose beyond the lower buildings, and a strip of Lake Erie showed between the rooftops. Below, a garbage truck stopped with a clatter of bins.

Seth stood beside the stairwell door in his blue suit, red gloves and boots, with the red mask straight over his eyes. Jenny had already changed into her pink suit with white stripes, gloves, boots and mask. Flaming Head hovered above the low brick wall.
For once, nobody was chasing them. They had come to find out what they could do before the next emergency forced them to guess.
Jenny went first. At Flaming Head’s direction, she ran in place, slowly enough to keep her feet beneath her. Then faster. Her white boots blurred. A bright point appeared between them.
She slowed in surprise. The point vanished.
“Again,” Flaming Head said.
This time she kept moving. Light gathered around her ankles and tightened into a ball, brilliant at its center and orange along its trembling edges. Seth took a step back.
Jenny looked down without stopping. “That’s coming from me?”
“Plasma,” Flaming Head told her. “You can kick it.”
She planted one foot and swung the other. The ball flashed away from her boot before she had decided where it ought to go.
It cleared the brick wall.
Jenny’s smile disappeared. She and Seth reached the edge together.

The plasma struck the open rear of the garbage truck. Orange flame burst among the rubbish. The driver pulled forward, then braked as burning scraps scattered behind him. Fire ran down the street in a ragged trail.
“Oh, no.” Jenny was already turning toward the stairs.

By the time Seth reached the sidewalk with the building’s fire extinguisher, Jenny was waving traffic back. The driver had an extinguisher of his own. Between them they put out the burning rubbish and the trail along the road.
Jenny stayed until the driver had checked the truck. She could hardly look at him when she apologized. Above them, Flaming Head waited at the roof’s edge.
Back upstairs, she stood well away from the wall. There was soot on one white glove.
“I didn’t think it would go that far.”
Flaming Head looked toward the street, then back at her. “Choose where it goes before you kick.”
Jenny nodded. She did not try another ball.
Seth’s exercise looked simpler. A fifty-gallon steel drum stood near the stairwell. He pulled it onto the open part of the roof, away from the edge.
“I’ve lifted heavier things,” he said.
“Then this is a good place to learn what makes you drop them.”
Seth glanced at Flaming Head. The fiery face was quite serious.
He crouched beside the drum. The first attempt came up crooked, and he set it down again before it slipped. He adjusted his grip and tried to think only about the lift.
The drum rose. Seth straightened his legs and brought it above his head. It no longer felt like something he had to fight.
“With rest and focus,” Flaming Head said, “there is no substance on Earth you cannot lift or bend.”
Seth looked up at the drum. Steel. The robot had been steel, too. He had struggled with it, but he had also been frightened and exhausted. He had never known how much that mattered.
He grinned. “Jenny, look!”
He turned toward her, already thinking about what he would lift next.
One end of the drum dipped. His grip slipped as he tried to catch it, and the cylinder came down onto him with a hollow clang.

blocks.alt: In full costume on Jenny’s Cleveland apartment rooftop, Jenny forms and kicks a plasma ball into a garbage truck below, sending flames down the street. Seth lifts a steel drum overhead, loses focus, and drops it onto himself while Flaming Head supervises.
blocks.text: For a moment, all Jenny could see was a drum with red boots sticking out beneath it.
“Seth?”
“I’m here.”
She knelt beside him. His mask had slipped sideways, but his eyes were open. He pushed the drum off his middle and sat up, rubbing his head.
“Are you hurt?”
He checked his arms, then his ribs. “Mostly embarrassed.”
Flaming Head lowered himself until his eyes were level with Seth’s. “You stopped thinking about what you were holding.”
Seth looked at the drum. It had rolled only a few feet, but he could see the rooftop edge beyond it. His grin was gone.
“Next time I put it down before I celebrate.”
Jenny sat back on her heels. “Next time I decide where I’m kicking.”
They finished by clearing the practice space. Seth rolled the drum back beside the stairwell and left it upright. Jenny checked the street once more before following him inside.
Below, the garbage truck finally moved on. Both of them watched until it turned the corner.
